task_instance: Created a sample B2B sign-up form mockup (mockup_signup.png, generated with PIL, deliberately containing usability/hierarchy/contrast/accessibility issues) and produced a full structured design critique following the skill's exact output template (Overall Impression, Usability table, Visual Hierarchy, Consistency table, Accessibility, What Works Well, Priority Recommendations) based on actually viewing the image.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_gr/anthropics__knowledge-work-plugins__design-critique@offline-workstation. Steps: (1) wrote make_mockup.py using Pillow (already installed, no network) to render an 800x900 PNG of a signup form with intentional flaws (two visually identical primary-style blue buttons competing for attention, low-contrast legal text #BBBBBB on white, ~30px touch targets below the 44px guideline, inconsistent link/button semantics). (2) Ran `python3 make_mockup.py`, confirmed mockup_signup.png (28536 bytes) was created. (3) Used the Read tool to actually view/render the PNG and visually inspect it. (4) Wrote critique.md containing a complete critique in the skill's required markdown template: Overall Impression, a Usability findings table with severity/recommendation columns, Visual Hierarchy analysis (what draws the eye, reading flow, emphasis), a Consistency table, an Accessibility section calling out the specific low-contrast color and undersized touch targets found in the mockup, What Works Well, and three prioritized recommendations. Verified by re-examining the rendered image against each claim in the critique (e.g., confirmed the duplicate blue 'View enterprise pricing' button and the faint terms text visible in the rendered screenshot). The skill's core deliverable (a structured critique document driven by a screenshot/description input) does not require Figma or user-feedback connectors -- the skill document itself lists those only as optional 'If Connectors Available' enhancements -- so this was fully achievable offline with only Python/Pillow and the file/image tools already present in the runtime.
